notes.title: 78th anniversary, with the Korean version and the theme song released.
notes.notes:
Taipei, Taiwan - The digital adaptation of the popular board game "Raid on Taihoku" is now available on Steam. Set in Japanese-occupied Taiwan in 1945, the game allows players to control an amnesiac female high school student and a Taiwan Dog as they embark on an adventure in a city ravaged by the US Army bombings. In the process of getting back her memories, she also encounters unexpected threats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/56c4a72d5245b39690398990fe2378cccd06b3c0.png[/img]
Raid on Taihoku is now launching its Korean version coinciding with the 78th anniversary of the historical event.

On May 31, 1945, over a hundred American bombers conducted a devastating airstrike on Taipei, resulting in severe casualties. This year marks the 78th anniversary of the event, and the Korean version will be released in late May.

Producer CHANG, SHAO-LIAN expressed that the Korean translation was undertaken by a team of 42 individuals led by Assistant Professor LEE, Jung-Min from Chinese Culture University (CCU), known as "Team BPMF." The translation process took three months to complete.

Assistant Professor LEE, Jung-Min is a prominent scholar in the field of comparative literature with a strong interest in colonial history. After playing "Raid on Taihoku," he was highly impressed and believed it to be excellent research material. As a result, he proposed the idea of translating the game into Korean to the production team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/0183ce438f2bf0b316c92cab782d0c878534ea8c.jpg[/img]
Team BPMF led by Assistant Professor LEE, Jung-Min

Professor LEE further explained that both Korea and Taiwan were both former Japanese colonies, but their perspectives on this historical period differ. Koreans tend to adopt a more negative stance, while Taiwanese lean towards discussing this part of history from a more positive angle. Due to the lack of understanding among many Koreans regarding Taiwanese perspectives, Professor LEEbelieves that "Raid on Taihoku" has the potential to serve as an opportunity for Koreans to gain insights into the Taiwanese viewpoint. He hopes this game will help Korean players deepen their understanding of Taiwan.

Coinciding with the 78th anniversary of the Raid on Taihoku, the MV for the game's theme song, "When The Sky Returned," written by musician Enno Cheng, has also been released. Enno Cheng expressed how the protagonist, Kiyoko, constantly stares into space as if looking into a distant past inspired her. Through this song, she aims to bring back the voices emanating from a faraway memory for her listeners, inviting the players to the game and the emotions it brings.

"When The Sky Returned" MV link: https: //youtu.be/JUPCozcOoCI

"Raid on Taihoku" was developed by Mizogames and Fun2 Studio and published by Loftstar Interactive Entertainment. It is now available on Steam and ready for interested players to join the experience.

notes.title: Raid on Taihoku is launched. Close to 50% of the players are international!
notes.notes:
Adapted from a popular board game, Raid on Taihoku will be officially launched on Steam at 8p.m. on Feb 15th!

The story is based in Taipei City under Japanese colonial rule in 1945. Players will be an amnestic high school girl, Kiyoko, and a Taiwanese dog, Kuro, to survive in the city under the raid by the United States Air Force. While Kiyoko is regaining her memories, they are also facing unexpected danger and challenges.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/7dd067bb39fef70fc3946459ee1f0a0ef96444a7.png[/img]
[i]Dadaocheng-bombed mansion[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/b355a983dd669014e44eb17e6a261a6912d0a61c.png[/img]
[i]Surrounded by cats, a girl with a bad attitude towards Kiyoko[/i]

Our producer, KJ Chang, indicates that only half of the players who have added the game into our wish lists are Taiwanese, and up to 47% of them are international. Next to Taiwanese players, the second biggest audience are Japanese players, and then those from the United States, China and Hong Kong.

Additionally, KJ Chang suggests that suffering from the raids is a shared memory of Japanese and Taiwanese people during WWII. To understand Japanese players’ thoughts more precisely, the team has also invited several Japanese who live in Taiwan to play the demo, including Prf. Kameda Toshi, who teaches in the Department of Japanese Language and Literature at National Taiwan University, and an international student Yamada Ryota, who studies in the Department of Chinese Literature at NTU. After playing the demo, they had an interview which was recorded as a short clip.

Prf. Kameda comes from Akita-ken, Japan, and has worked in Taiwan for 8 years. His hometown, Tsuchizaki Port, was also under raid during the war. He praised Raid on Taihoku from the perspective of a Japanese scholar. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/c9844e27e14a69ba5bbc35a983c4516ba45b7265.png[/img]
[i]Kiyoko, rescuing people in the sea of ​​fire[/i]

Coming from Okinawa, Japan, Yamada Ryota has studied in Taiwan for almost 4 years. He said that Okinawa was seriously damaged in WWII.  Noticing the Japanese remains while living here in Taiwan, he could therefore feel the deep connection between the two countries, and he also learned more about the unfamiliar stories from Raid on Taihoku. 

Moreover, the college mentioned above, National Taiwan University, correlates to Japan itself. It was established in 1928 (Showa 3), originally named “Taihoku Imperial University,” as one of the nine imperial universities founded by the Empire of Japan. The affiliated “Taihoku Hospital” has also been shown in the game. The team aspires to grant players the most immersive playing experience while pursuing the apocalyptic aesthetics and remaining true to the historical facts. 

[url=https://youtu.be/yNfTwjoeJ9w]【Raid on Taihoku】PC game trailer[/url]

To commemorate May 31st, the day of the Taipei Air Raid, the game "Taipei Air Raid" is priced at NT$531, with a 10% discount for the first week of listing. There is also an official artbook and original soundtrack available for purchase. The official artbook contains a wealth of concept art and plot illustrations such as characters, scenes, and collections. The original soundtrack, composed by well-known musicians WeiFan Chang and Enno Cheng, contains 29 soundtracks in line with the situation of the times and the game's ending song, "The End of the War". The game also launched a deluxe bundle package, which allows players to fully collect the "Taipei Air Raid" video game, art setting collection, and original soundtrack at a  15% discount.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/e99869e7cfb2d7fc7c09338cf9c4c6f103ebdc35.png[/img]
[i]the two people talking at a shrine[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/ef5516524ebfeb11fdf397c1b0639c41287e46a1.png[/img]
[i]Looking at Taipei City from Taiwan Shrine (now the Grand Hotel)[/i]

Raid on Taihoku is produced by Mizo Games, Fun2 Studio, launched by Loftstar Interactive Entertainment. It will be officially launched on Steam on February 16th. Welcome the players who are interested in experiencing the game with us.

notes.title: Those who forgot about war, welcome to the world of human cannibalism
notes.notes:
[b][h3]Adapted from a popular board game, Raid on Taihoku will be officially launched on Steam on Feb, 16th. The one-minute trailer is released, as well as many playing clips. [/h3][/b]
In the game, a player can control the amnestic Kiyoko and the Taiwanese dog, Kuro, playing the game with dual roles. In addition to Kiyoko’s lost memories, still lots of puzzles are waiting for the players to solve. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/287d4f0bd9239e70bf78fb0e86417d11bef7c92f.png[/img]

From the trailer videos, we can see that besides evading the raid, a player can also put out fires, secretly track someone or confront a SHP, Special Higher Police. There are even some impacting scenes such as prisoners kneeling on the ground while being punished and beaten in the game. 

All the settings in Taihoku in the game have been released, too. The delicate modeling authentically reconstructs the Taipei City under Japanese colonial rule.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/f0770365969cc6e93fd74191a756c4a28ace45a4.png[/img]

[b][h3]After the demo version was released in last June, the team took the players advices and enhanced the game, focusing the concept on “the helplessness under a war,” and increasing the collections responding to the plot.[/h3][/b]
 One of the new collections is the leading role Kiyoko’s monologue, reflecting her changing feelings in a war. At the same time, the dialogue has been adjusted, and the team also renewed Kiyoko’s and Blacky’s Tachies, as well as the other characters’ facial features. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/8f322b4efcfa3625488e27af12c585607f077d68.png[/img]

There are over 50 original sountracks of the game, because we hope all the players can really immerse themselves in the game as if they are in a war. In addition to the dual roles, there are still other important roles such as the priest, the SHP, the geisha, the doctor, the thief and so on. 

Raid on Taihoku is produced by Mizo Games, Fun2 Studio, launched by Loftstar Interactive Entertainment, and will be officially launched in English, Japanese and Chinese on Steam. If you are interested in it, please add it in your wish list on Steam and catch up the latest news about the game.

notes.title: Not for dogs this time! Raid on Taihoku is back again!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/61944ad4ea11f89aef2fa7d9e44e46b62ca08406.jpg[/img]

On Feb, 16, 2023, the video game Raid on Taihoku will be officially released on Steam. Thank you for your patience and long waiting. We sincerely invite you to share the good news with your friends, and together add it in the game list on Steam!

Raid on Taihoku is a 2.5 D narrative adventure game, based on the city of Taihoku, under Japanese colonial rule and the raid of United States Air Force. The story is about how an amnesia high school girl, Sayako, and a Taiwanese dog, Blacky, try to survive in their adventure. While evading the raid, Sayako gradually regains her memories, but in the meanwhile, she finds out the appalling past…

With  our team’s several tests and updates, the game has been all set and ready. We wish to make you feel closer to the suffered ones in wars via our game. 

[h3]Released after Chinese New Year, the game has reached its best version within our limited time and sources. [/h3]
Raid on Taihoku is neither a 3A epic-like game, nor a masterpiece with astonishing Gameplay, but it is rather an independent game, which focuses on the balance of factual history and sentiments. Through the game, we want to make the players empathize with the pain and suffering brought by warfare. 

The game includes historical scenes such as Taiwan Sotokufu (today’s Presidential Office), Taiwan Grand Shrine (today’s Grand Hotel), Taihoku Hospital (today’s National Taiwan University Hospital), Taihoku Station (dismantled), Penglai Catholic Church (ruined in the raid), Manka Longshan Temple, Dadaocheng and so on, with a view to represent our beautiful home, Taiwan, before it was threatened by the war. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/f4cb57daf239c844564e0d55cb7672d318f0d911.jpg[/img]

[h3]More than 50 soundtracks in Raid on Taihoku[/h3]
Before officially releasing the game, we hope to embrace more players’ advices. Therefore, we are going to hold a two-week-long white paper test in December, whose participants include Japanese players, and even Japanese professors. We will dedicatedly polish and enhance the game by accepting these feedbacks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/ab2ae66f3a3a5b22415ba7563816060bb73aa8ba.jpg[/img]

Thanks again for your support and understanding. We want to present you the best version of the game, hoping that it will also meet your expectations.

Though the ashes still linger on the European land and the fire ruins Ukraine, we hope in this unstable generation, warfare can only be seen in the game. 

Sincerely, 
Team of Raid on Taihoku

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/f5002291951799e807aee077633f221d2fe4bedc.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Looking Back on the Taiwanese History with Raid on Taihoku - Taiwan Grand Shrine
notes.notes:
Taiwan Grand Shrine was constructed in 1901. It was built to honor Prince Kitashirakawa Yoshihisa who passed away in Taiwan in 1895. Taiwan Grand Shrine was ranked the highest Japanese Shinto shrine in Taiwan during Japanese occupation. It was severely burned and damaged by a crashed plane during the raid on Taihoku, and was torn down after WWII. It is now the Grand Hotel’s current location.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/493c89d6ccf803ed2cdfb48e2df906fbeec81414.jpg[/img]

Although Taiwan Grand Shrine is no longer in existence, some of its materials are still kept until today.  A part of the Torii in Taiwan Grand Shrine is now reconstructed as the Dragon Pillar of Sanxia Qingshui Zushi Temple located in Taipei. The copper bull at the entrance of Taiwan Grand Shrine was relocated to the gate of National Taiwan Museum. A pair of lion-dogs is now standing at the center of Jiantan Park, guarding the citizens in the area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/820fa02be1579292138bcb7210a0f4641d419699.png[/img]

Taiwan Grand Shrine is an important scene in the game. What events await for Kiyoko on the way to Taiwan Grand Shrine? What does Taiwan Grand Shrine mean to Kiyoko?

notes.title: Where Did Kuro Come From? Let’s Talk about Taiwan Dog
notes.notes:
Dogs are the most faithful friends of humans. Taiwan Dog especially possesses a faithful image to people.
 The Taiwan Dog Kuro in the game has a red collar on his neck. He is extremely smart and active, and is capable of executing commands from the player. Kuro is now separated from his/her owner, and is specifically friendly and kind to Kiyoko. Why exactly is that the case?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/0bd3aa05795b1d61b90c1699f1bda1bd718880c7.png[/img]

The prototype of Kuro is actually a Taiwan Dog named Taroke. Taroke is also the pet of the producer KJ. He is now 3 years old, and has a great passion in eating and talking walks. If there is a benchmark in being cute, Taroke will be ranked in the top tier. The team took great amount of observations and researches on Taroke’s body movement during the process of modeling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/68f9560d000c1965cbf5be4985bd513aafa1fec0.jpg[/img]
Image: Taroke

Speaking of Taiwan Dog, some will call them Taiwanese mutt. They are the most common local breed in Taiwan. Taiwan Dog possesses a faithful and courageous character. They were often trained as retrievers in the past. In modern times, people also breed them as guarding and companion dogs.
Do you have a faithful and courageous dog in your house? More stories on Kuro the Taiwan Dog awaits players to explore in “Raid on Taihoku”.

notes.title: Looking Back the History of Taiwan with Raid on Taihoku - the Very First Catholi
notes.notes:
Built in 1914, Horaicho Catholic Church is the very first Catholic church in Taipei. It would have witnessed over one hundred years of history if it still exists. The church was built in gothic architecture, with a spectacular 30 meters high bell tower in the center of the building. Unfortunately, the church was bombed and destroyed during the raid on Taihoku.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/2c5656c8a9f817570e9ea82419b94fd075717038.jpg[/img]
Image: Wikipedia

The church was rebuilt at No. 245, Minsheng W. Rd., Datong Dist., Taipei City after WWII. It is now the headquarters of The Taipei Catholic Cathedral of The Immaculate Conception. The church is neighboring the Catholic building - Blessed Imelda's School. There is also a kindergarten placed right next to the church.

The destroyed church is an iconic scene in the game. The protagonist Kiyoko wakes up next to the damaged building, learning that she was placed in a pile of bodies. It seems that she was disposed as a victim of the raid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/c817c04e5a0a94a232ed469ee725be5583117966.jpg[/img]

Kiyoko finds out that she has lost her memory. Father Takeda, the person who is in charge of the church, is a kind Japanese priest. It looks like he knows Kiyoko, but somehow cannot give a clear explanation on the past of Kiyoko and her parents' whereabouts. Does he really have no information on this, or is he hiding something?

notes.title: Air Raid Alert! How Much Do You Know about the Bomb Shelters in Taiwan
notes.notes:
During the period of Japanese occupation, in order to survive from the air bombardment carried out by the U.S. military, there were bomb shelters built across Taiwan. To name a few that were actually visited by Mizo Games, Taiwan Literature Base in Taipei, Ciaotou Sugar Refinery in Kaohsiung, and the trench in National Keelung Girls' Senior High School. Keelung has the most shelters across the entire Taiwan, with 682 of them in place.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/8cd882fe9d5bcc3efd0f1dcc5f47be3a99e22fc9.png[/img]

Government of Taiwan during the period of Japanese occupation (the modern day Presidential Palace) was also half-destroyed by the air bombardment. The building was also designed with bomb shelters in place. The civilian staff that worked in the building was killed by the air raid on May 31st, 1945. According to a friend’s grandmother of the studio, the only scene that was left looking from the Shezidao was a sea of flames. The grandmother, who was only a young girl at the time, heard the news that her brother was killed during the air raid. She walked a long way from Shezidao to the building of the Government of Taiwan, looking for the body of her own brother by the side of the air shelter. Ironically, the air shelter that was supposed to protect people has collapsed and eternally separated them from their loved ones. Instead, those who couldn’t make it into the shelter have survived and told the grandmother the unfortunate news.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/30b938d9588af9a98ab46ce00fd8d74381f6a002.png[/img]

We try to rebuild the scenes and stories that we actually visited and heard and integrate them into Raid on Taihoku. In the game, Kiyoko, the protagonist, is forced to jump in a bomb shelter in order to avoid the deteriorating bombardments. As people stay in the dark shelter, listening to the sound of bombs coming from the outside, they become more and more restless.
The fate ahead that awaits Kiyoko will only be discovered by the players.

notes.title: The Very First Department Store in Taiwan - Kikumoto Hyakkaten
notes.notes:
In Raid on Taihoku, in addition to bringing the players to witness the cruelty of war and the struggles of the relationship between people, we hope to help players to learn Taiwanese history from different perspectives. Players will be able to see historical sites and landmarks in Taihoku during the period of Japanese occupation. Some of them were completely destroyed by the ruthless war and are now beyond anyone’s recognition. Others were seen as important historical buildings, but were unable to acquire a formal recognition of their historical status and failed to gain the much-needed protection due to various reasons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/b1975452feb75a15e6e935f2eed8bb327bd34858.png[/img]

The department store “Kikumoto Hyakkaten” was one of the historical buildings under such condition. It was built in the year of 1932, and was located in Taipei Sakaemachi Street (the intersection between Hengyang Road and Boai Road in modern day Taipei). It was the very first department store in Taiwan. The building was 6 stories high, with a watchtower built on top. It was nicknamed as “the Seventh Heaven” due to its height. Kikumoto Hyakkaten had the signature facility of a modernized building – elevators, in place. It was located in the heart of Taihoku, with Japanese customers as the primary visitors. Therefore, the merchandise inside was mainly imported luxury goods, resulting in Kikumoto Hyakkaten being seen as an important pop culture showcase floor in Taiwan.

Until this day, the owners of Kikumoto Hyakkaten shifted multiple times. Sadly, the very first department store in Taiwan was unable to acquire a formal monument status from the Taipei City Government. The building is only identified as a “historical building”. Therefore, the authority cannot prevent the owner of the building from reconstructing it. There are a number of cultural and historical workers, dedicating to file an appeal on the authority, with the hope to do their part in the preservation of historical buildings. If Kikumoto Hyakkaten could be more actively repaired and preserved, instead of being kept only in texts or images, it can deliver a more meaningful cultural value.

notes.title: Raid on Taihoku - Bring You Back to Taipei, 1945
notes.notes:
At the end of WWII, the U.S. performed the “island hopping” strategy on Japan. Two countries were in an aerial combat in the sky above Taiwan Strait.
May 31st, 1945, A total of 117 B-24 bombers fly towards the capital of Taiwan - Taihoku (Taipei).

Based on historical records, the U.S. military performed countless bombing runs on Taihoku, causing heavy casualties. A terrifying amount of people were killed by the bombardments, and those who survived, lost their homes. Many world-renowned historical sites were also flattened by the ruthless war.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/107d3b3e3ef8b69f2da71a9a67a1543f2d770a2b.jpg[/img]

The heavy bombardment brought by the U.S. military was without a doubt a severe hit on Taihoku. It also brought deep impacts on the infrastructure development in the future Taipei. The modern day Office of the President was the Taiwan Soutokufu (Government of Taiwan), and was directly hit by a bomb from the U.S bombardment. The front of the building and the side of the tower were severely damaged, and the building was not fully repaired until the year of 1948. Even until this day, there is still a part of the building that can’t be fully restored. The modern day Legislative Yuan (the parliament) on the other side was acting as the Agricultural Office and Forestry Bureau, and was used as the dormitory of Taipei Second Girls’ High School. The dormitory section was also severely damaged by the bombardment, leaving only the brick walls standing. The school was unfortunately abandoned afterwards due to the difficulty of repairing and lack of staff. There are many other priceless historical buildings that were destroyed by the ruthless war and beyond anyone’s recognition. People can only imagine the scene through history records. We hope through the form of video games, we can take players around the globe to dust off this part of the Taiwanese history that was long buried in the stream of time.

The player’s in-game adventure takes place in the severely bombed Taihoku in WWII, including the shady streets of Dadaocheng, the decayed Sakae Town Shopping Street, the dangerous Taihoku Train Station, the Taiwan Soutokufu that was targeted by the U.S. military, and also the Cathedral of Taipei and the abandoned Taiwan Shrine that were nearly completed destroyed. Despite many scenes that only remained in old photographs and memories, they will make a beautiful comeback in a brand new form in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/22f57e97b4087a097f19fc530378d146eded5830.jpg[/img]

We craft with the finest quality, and we invite you back to the year 1945 to witness a war-torn Taipei that you have never seen before.
The past cannot be rewound, but the memory can be rebuilt. In the unstable generation, we wish you all the best with everything.

notes.title: Raid on Taihoku Steam Page is Now Officially Online
notes.notes:
[h3]All wars are fought twice, the first time on the battlefield, the second time in memory.[/h3]

Hi everyone, we are Mizo Games!
“Let the world acknowledge Taiwan is the responsibility of our generation.”
From board game to video game, we’ve always kept that spirit in mind, hoping to get more people to learn the different aspects of Taiwanese history.
 
The game is derived from Mizo Games' proudest original board game creation. It is also the very first Taiwanese video game that sets the backdrop in World War II Taiwan.

Back to the year of 1945, as a young girl Kiyoko who suffers from amnesia, you will walk into the battle-scarred Taiwan at the end of WWII and try to survive in a war-torn city with a cute stray dog named Kuro.
 Aside from avoiding the heavy bombardments from the sky, you will witness the tragic development from the characters and experience the struggles of human nature. Through the game, you will deeply experience the ruthlessness of war and the cruelty of reality.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42023174/a7212a30a2782fd991afc3efd263f5a78d1cc881.jpg[/img]

Today, we are gladly announcing that the store page of “Raid on Taihoku” is now officially open!
Our team will release a Demo version of our game and more information regarding the stage of the development in the upcoming future. Wishlist now and stay tuned for our latest news!
